spots.name: Karlsruhe Palace
spots.summary: Karlsruhe Palace was built in 1715 for Margrave Charles III William of Baden-Durlach after a dispute with the citizens of his previous capital, Durlach. The city of Karlsruhe has since grown around it. The building is now home to the main museum of the Badisches Landesmuseum.

spots.name: Karlsruhe Pyramid
spots.summary: The Karlsruhe Pyramid is a pyramid made of red sandstone, located in the centre of the market square of Karlsruhe, Germany. It was erected in the years 1823–1825 over the vault of the city's founder, Margrave Charles III William (1679–1738).

spots.name: Karlsruhe Zoo
spots.summary: The Karlsruhe Zoo is a city garden with a zoo in the southwest of Karlsruhe, Germany. It also encompasses the outer area; Tierpark Oberwald in the southeast of the city. The main area totals 22 hectares, and the Oberwald Zoo has an area of 16 hectares.

spots.summary: The Staatliche Kunsthalle is an fine art museum in Karlsruhe, Germany. Its collection consists of works by mainly German, French, Flemish and Dutch masters from the past eight centuries.

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The State Museum of Natural History Karlsruhe, abbreviated SMNK, is one of the two state of Baden-Württemberg's natural history museums. Together with the State Museum of Natural History Stuttgart it is one of the most important repositories for state-owned natural history collections.

spots.summary: The Botanischer Garten Karlsruhe is a municipal botanical garden located in Karlsruhe, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. This garden should not be confused with the nearby Botanical Garden of the KIT operated by the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT).

spots.name: Schlossgarten
spots.summary: The Karlsruhe Schlossgarten, also called Schlosspark, is a landscape park situated north of the Karlsruhe Palace in the center of Karlsruhe. It represents an extension of the palace grounds to the north, serves the people as a local holiday spot and is regularly used for events.

spots.name: Hauptfriedhof Karlsruhe
spots.summary: The Hauptfriedhof in Karlsruhe is one of the oldest German communal rural cemeteries. In 1871, the first plans to build a new burial ground outside the city center began.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Karlsruhe Synagogue was a Jewish congregation and synagogue, located in Karlsruhe, in the state of Baden-Württemberg, Germany. Designed by Friedrich Weinbrenner in the Egyptian Revival style, the synagogue was completed in 1798 and demolished in 1871.

spots.name: Scruffy's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Scruffy's is Karlsruhe's best Irish Pub. The interior of the bar is reminiscent of the hold of an old ship and is a comfortable environment. There are a variety of beers and whiskeys, as well as good Irish music every week. Often the owner's band will play, always a treat. The bartenders and some of the patrons are native English speakers, so it's a good place to let the tourist's brain relax afte

spots.name: Z-10

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A bar run by local university students that is frequented by the Karlsruhe's student population. There are several local beers offered here for very cheap (€1-1.50) and also decent cocktails. Bands are frequently playing on Saturdays (no entry fee) and visitors can play cards, board games and table soccer with other patrons. Check the website for hours as the bar is generally only open when school

spots.name: Dorfschänke

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Dorfschänke is Karlsruhe's oldest Kneipe, and a good place to meet up with people. With the normal selection of beers and drinks, this is also a good place to see bands or to watch soccer outside during the summer. There is also a fairly popular "Kicker" (or Foos-ball) table inside where you can pick up a game or two. Be prepared to pay cover on nights when bands are playing.

spots.name: Café Bleu

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Restaurant owned by the same purveyor that runs "Die Kippe". It has the same menu as Die Kippe, but different atmospheres. Both restaurants are always a nice place to grab breakfast, a drink with friends, or a quick meal without breaking the bank.

spots.name: Badisch Brauhaus

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A very large multi-storey beer garden, brewery and restaurant. On its uppermost floor is a cocktail bar; probably the nicest place in Karlsruhe for cocktails (although on weekends it can be difficult to get a seat and service can be slow).

spots.name: Alter Brauhof

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A nice place to sit outside and have a beer (only a good place in summer), also offers decent food. It's not so well known, so you stand a good chance of finding a nice place even on a nice summer evening even on weekends.

spots.name: Vogelbräu Karlsruhe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A beer garden, restaurant and brewery. You get good beer and German food here, really a nice place for lunch, dinner or drinking. There are two more 'Vogelbräu' restaurants in the nearby towns of Ettlingen and Durlach.

spots.name: Dean&David

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A very modern franchise restaurant that strives to offer healthy fast-food from fresh ingredients. It offers mostly curries, soups and a large selection of salads.
